newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Tadiran wins Asian army radio contract.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Tadiran wins Asian army radio contract.

text.p: Tadiran Communications Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Tadiran Ltd, said it had won a contract for military radio-telephones from an unnnamed Asian government.
Tadiran said the first phase of the contract, which it won as a sub-contractor for GTE Corp of the U.S., was worth $5 million. It said it expected to win a further $30 million in orders from it.
A Tadiran spokeswoman said the company could not identify the buyer for political reasons. The contract was won in the framework of the U.S. government's Foreign Military Support (FMS) programme.

Lior Almagor, Tadiran Communications' deputy managing director for marketing, said in a statement that Asian armies are beginning to make significant purchases of military communications equipment after a long slow period.
He said he hoped the current contract would lead to more orders, enabling Tadiran Communications to win a big portion of the developing market.
Tadiran Communications said its total orders backlog stood at $280 million.
